messages:
alex: Heads-up — DSAR SR-2026-412 just came in (acme@example.com). They want full deletion. We're planning KMS rotation this week for the embeddings keystore. Does rotation block the deletion workflow? need clarity on RBAC/service-account path. cc @maria

maria: Short answer: rotation shouldn't inherently block deletes, but there are edge cases. Need to confirm whether our delete flow requires decrypting wrapped keys vs just removing metadata + triggering snapshot purge. What's the DSAR id?

alex: SR-2026-412 (privacy portal). Current mental model: API -> mark delete -> enqueue -> backfill worker calls keystore to destroy wrapped key + triggers snapshot purge (ttl=0). If old wrapping key is disabled/rotated, the destroy/unwrap might fail.

sam: If wrapped key cannot be unwrapped we can still mark the customer record deleted and remove vectors from the index. BUT for legal evidence we prefer a crypto-delete path (proof-of-destruction). Worker needs kms:Decrypt and kms:Destroy permissions on that key/version. Service account RBAC is critical.

maria: @sam +1. Two practical mitigations: (1) delay rotation until DSAR backlog for that key is clear, or (2) adopt a retire-then-destroy model where we revoke compute access (so data inaccessible) then schedule actual crypto-shred once deletions finished. Also need audit entries for every step.

jordan: Ops note: the snapshot retention/purge job runs out of a different GCP project. Ensure cross-project service account (snapshot-purge-sa) is in the KMS key IAM bindings. We had an incident 3w ago where the purge job couldn't access the key because IAM drift removed the role.

alex: For DSAR response we need two things: a) a fallback if crypto-destroy fails that still meets legal requirements, and b) an audit-proof bundle we can hand to legal without keeping plaintext. Any thoughts on a minimal proof design?

maria: Proposal sketch: on DSAR submit mark items with tag `pending_erasure`. Immediately run index purge + metadata wipe. For key material, instead of immediate destroy, rotate to "detached" state (remove SA roles so compute can't use it) and keep key material for a short retention window until purge confirms. Then perform crypto-shred/destroy and record signed operation log (operator SA, timestamps, key version, operation hashes). Produce a proof bundle (hashes + signed log).

sam: Quick staging test idea & pseudo CLI to reproduce flow:
```
# revoke SA access
gcloud projects remove-iam-policy-binding my-prod --member=serviceAccount:dsar-worker@... --role=roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter
# destroy a key version
gcloud kms keys versions destroy --location=global --keyring=redwood-kr --key=embeds-key --version=3
```
We'll need to validate error modes & that destroy produces audit entries. I'll run in staging and paste logs.

privacy-bot: Ticket created: PRIV-412-A (SR-2026-412) — assigned to @maria. Checklist: index purge, metadata wipe, key access revoke, crypto-shred, proof bundle.

jordan: :eyes: I'll add cross-project SA checks into infra-as-code and a pre-rotation validation that queries pending DSARs for affected key ids. Also suggest an automated alert if a KMS rotation is scheduled within 7 days of a DSAR touching that key.

alex: Two asks from legal/privacy side: (1) eng-sec to produce an "erasure proof" template (signed hashes + op timestamps + operator SA + evidence of index purge) and (2) infra to gate or at least warn on KMS rotations for keys with pending DSAR flags. If gating is hard, a hard warning is acceptable.

maria: Will draft the erasure proof template (signed operation log + hashes + linked audit IDs). For gating: we can add a rotation-policy plugin to the rotation pipeline that calls the DSAR service endpoint to check for pending flags. I'll open a PR tomorrow; aiming for EOD Fri for the initial check.

sre-oncall: If useful I can add a lightweight /ops-check endpoint that returns pending DSAR count per key id so rotation automation can call it without hitting privacy DB directly.

alex: Great — @sam please validate destroy path in staging and share the logs. I'll tell legal the interim mitigation: mark as deleted + index purge + revoke key access until crypto-shred completes.

maria: :+1:
